description: Creation of enlarged parking area involving new hardstand, wheelchair access ramp and replacement entrance gates with a maximum height of 1.2 meters.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:GA150GA100GA110Heritage, Design and Access StatementGA001Sustainable Drainage and Flood Risk AssessmentGA510GA500Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Unless otherwise specified in the application the materials to be used for the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted along with work of making good shall be carried out in materials to match those of the existing building. Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development respects the appearance, existing materials and built and natural features of the surrounding area.

Prior to installation of the gate and posts hereby approved, detailed drawings, including elevations and material specifications, of the new timber gate and posts shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The gate shall be of a traditional rural design, such as a simple timber five-bar or comparable farmer's gate style, to complement the rural character of the area. The approved details shall be implemented and retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure the development preserves the character and appearance of the Forty Hill Conservation Area.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans, prior to completion or first occupation of the development hereby approved, whichever is the sooner; full details of all proposed tree planting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include:a)	Planting and aftercare specifications, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or other protective measures and confirmation of locations;b)	species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier and defect period. All tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times;c)	tree pit design (where appropriate) and;d)	underground modular systems (where appropriate).Any trees that are found to be dead, dying, severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced in the next planting season by specimens of similar size and species in the first suitable planting season. Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with the Biodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and the Publication London Plan.

The site shall be landscaped in accordance with the approved garden plan GA110 in the first planting season after completion, or prior to the occupation of the development, whichever is the sooner. Any existing trees and shrubs specified for retention, must be retained on the site. Any trees or shrubs which die or become severely damaged or diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced with new planting in accordance with the approved details.Reason: In the interest of the amenity of neighbours, to provide a satisfactory appearance and to ensure that the development does not prejudice highway safety.
